```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(IntegMultiReg)
```

`imr()` stores selection indicators and MRF interactions. To obtain regression
coefficients and residual variances, run `posterior_draws()` on the fit. This
starts a second-stage conditional calculation; it can take longer when many
distinct selection models were retained.

## A small continuous example

```{r fit}
x <- data.frame(id = 1:40, marker = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 40))
y <- data.frame(id = x$id, response = 1 + x$marker + sin(x$id) / 3)
fit <- imr(list(assay = x), y, type_outcome = "continuous", h0 = 1,
           sample_mcmc = c(500, 250), seed = 1)
post <- posterior_draws(fit, draws = 1000, burnin = 1000,
                        conditional_draws = 1000, chains = 2, seed = 2)
```

The returned `beta` matrices contain coefficient draws, including exact zeros
for inactive molecular features. The intercept and clinical coefficients stay
in every model. Slopes use the subgroup-standardized predictor scales.

```{r intervals}
confint(post)[[1]][, c("term", "mean", "lower", "upper")]
v <- post$variance[[1]]
rbind(variance = quantile(v, c(.025, .5, .975)),
      standard_deviation = quantile(sqrt(v), c(.025, .5, .975)))
post$diagnostics
```

These are Bayesian credible intervals. The `draws` argument controls the number
of returned model-average rows; `conditional_draws` sets the minimum retained
length of each conditional chain. Inspect `diagnostics` and increase the latter
and burn-in when the conditional chains do not explore adequately. Conditional
split R-hat concerns this second stage; it does not diagnose the selection chain.

## Conditional means and future observations

```{r prediction}
new <- list(assay = data.frame(id = 41, marker = 0))
predict(post, new, type = "mean")
predict(post, new, type = "response")
```

For continuous outcomes, `"mean"` describes uncertainty in the conditional
response mean. `"response"` also generates residual noise for a future outcome.
For binary outcomes, use `"mean"` for event-probability intervals; response
intervals are discrete zero/one intervals.

For a log-time survival fit, posterior predictions are transformed to time units
and summarized by medians. The fitted-object `predict(fit, ...)` method returns
working log-time point predictions. Future censoring times are not generated.

The conditional calculation inherits empirical selection weights from the
Laplace-based first stage. Good conditional diagnostics do not make these
weights exact. Complete conditional-chain trajectories and latent-response
draws are not retained in the public 0.1.3 result.
